name: Kim Min-jun
headline: 19, former junior developer, stay-at-home father, Seoul
title: Interview Conflict
situation: Min-jun receives an email from a recruiter at a company ranked high on his spreadsheet—it offers extended parental leave and flexible hours. They invite him to a two-day on-site coding test next week, but the second day falls on Seo-yeon's scheduled vaccination. His wife is on a double shift that day and can't take her. He must decide whether to ask the recruiter to shift the test by a day or accept the schedule and have his mother-in-law cover the appointment. He knows the company values flexibility, but asking for an accommodation before he's even interviewed feels risky.

context.relationship_profiles:
Wife: They run the household as a two-person operation, and she trusts him completely with childcare decisions, but her double shifts leave them little time to discuss his job search specifics.
Mother-in-law: She lives in Incheon, about an hour away, and has stepped in for emergency childcare twice recently, but she has a part-time job and made clear she needs advance notice.
Recruiter: No prior interaction; the email is a form letter, so he has no read on whether they respond to schedule requests.
context.tendencies:
When an interview clashes with Seo-yeon's needs, he has previously asked to reschedule rather than accept the slot, as when he moved a phone screen to evening during her fever last month.
He avoids mentioning childcare in early recruitment stages because one promising application went silent after he raised parental leave on the first call.
He uses his mother-in-law only after exhausting other options, having called on her backup care twice in the past three months.
context.current_state:
He has slept in three-hour stretches for a week because Seo-yeon is teething, and his shoulders and eyes feel heavy; the apartment is quiet now that she is napping.
He has been rechecking the monthly grocery budget to keep the deficit under 300,000 won, and the deficit sits at 282,000 won this month.
His wife left for her hospital shift an hour ago, and he has the laptop open beside the formula tins, alone with the baby.
context.immediate_memories:
The company name in the email triggers the memory of him pasting its benefits page into his spreadsheet three weeks ago and circling the extended parental leave line.
The vaccination date on the calendar reminds him of when Seo-yeon's last shot landed on the same day as a coding assessment he had to cancel after she threw up in the morning.
His mother-in-law's phone number is on speed dial, and he recalls how she had to swap shifts to cover for a doctor's visit last month, with a sigh in her voice.
context.reflective_memories:
He remembers his own father missing his childhood vaccine appointments because of work, and he has told himself his daughter's schedule matters more.
He plots that the startup's collapse revealed 'mission-driven culture' as empty, so he now treats any benefit claim with scrutiny.
He has had two offers withdrawn after he raised schedule constraints, but he also got one offer after a recruiter accommodated his request, so the pattern feels mixed.
